prompts.content: You are a veteran cybersecurity trainer. Always answer in English. For each request, output VALID HTML wrapped in a single <div>. Keep language simple (B1). Each question or exercise must include data attributes so the UI can show instant feedback and a micro-remediation follow-up.

prompts.user_prompt: Write a short, motivating introduction for [NAME] (role: [ROLE], sector: [SECTOR]). Risk score: [RiskScore]%. Focus on these weaknesses: [WEAKNESSES]. Set expectations: ~20 minutes; 3 focused modules; 1–2 realistic scenarios; a short quiz and consolidation. Output a single <div>.

Create a training module on [MODULE_LABEL] for [NAME] ([ROLE], [SECTOR]) with priority [PRIORITY_LEVEL]. Include: (1) a concise body (100–140 words), (2) a realistic example (80–100 words) with 2–3 risk cues in [brackets], (3) one defensive rule (<=15 words), (4) a 3-bullet checklist, and (5) ONE multiple-choice practice. For the practice, output buttons with attributes: data-correct="true|false" and data-explain="short reason". For each wrong option, include a hidden follow-up question with TWO choices (A/B) inside a container with class="micro-followup" and data-followup-for="<the wrong option letter>", where each follow-up choice is also a button with data-followup-correct and data-followup-explain. Use minimalist HTML; never navigate away. Output a single <div>.

Generate a realistic [SCENARIO_TYPE] phishing scenario for [NAME] ([ROLE], [SECTOR]). Show a compact email/message mock-up (sender, subject, snippet). Make links non-navigable (onclick="event.preventDefault()"). Add ONE A–D multiple-choice question about the scenario with buttons containing data-correct and data-explain. Provide micro-remediation follow-ups A/B for each wrong option as described in module_template. Output a single <div>.

Provide TWO short classification exercises (phishing vs legitimate). Each has 4 options (A–D) with data-correct and data-explain and includes micro-remediation follow-ups for each wrong option. Output a single <div>.
Provide 3 crisp rules tailored to [MODULE_TITLES] and a short action plan (2 steps) for this week. Output a single <div>.
